findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

1) An employee was observed to handle their phone and not wash their hands prior to resuming food service. 2) An employee was observed to change gloves without hand washing. 3) An employee was observed to touch their clothing and head without hand washing. 4) An employee was observed to have a drink and not wash their hands prior to resuming food service. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to refresh hand washing procedures (including when to wash hands) with all staff to prevent future issues. Wash hands whenever they are contaminated and prior to handling foods/food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the soap dispenser in the kitchen would not dispense for hand washing. The PIC was consulted and found that the batteries had been left out after the last refill of the dispenser. Batteries were added and the equipment was observed to function correctly after. Ensure that all hand sink supplies are maintained functional and available at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) The dish machine in the kitchen would not register effective levels of CL sanitizer when first checked. 2) (REPEAT) The bar dish machine was not observed to have effective levels of CL sanitizer for food contact surfaces during the inspection. Investigation of both locations showed a freshly changed jug of sanitizer concentrate and an empty line. The lines were primed and the machines registered correctly anfterwards. Education conducted.  Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple moist wiping cloths were observed left on the counters throughout the kitchen. The kitchen manager was shown and moved the cloths back to the sani buckets to correct. Ensure that all sani rags are stored between uses in the sani buckets.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Several locations of the ceiling heave major dust build up. The PIC was instructed to clean and maintain clean prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple employee drinks (Gatorade/C4) were observed on the counters on the back prep area without a lid/straw. Education was conducted and the drinks removed to correct. Ensure that employee beverages are maintained so that possible contamination of consumer foods/food contact areas is mitigated.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

An employee phone was observed on the cutting board of a prep cooler. A cut eggplant and knife were observed next to it as well as other foods being prepared. The PIC was shown and removed the phone to correct. The cutting board was sanitized as well. Ensure that employee belongings do not become a concern for contamination of foods and equipment.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without washing their hands in the kitchen area. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that hand washing is taking place when needed at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The bar dish machine was not observed to have effective levels of CL sanitizer for food contact surfaces during the inspection. The concentrate jug was changed by the PIC and still did not adjust to effective levels. A third jug was brought out and looked significantly more yellow than the previous fresh jug. Once primed this brought the effective concentration up to acceptable levels and corrected the violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The salad prep cooler was observed with internal temperatures for lettuce, cheeses and house made mayo based sauces are observed in the 51F-52F range. These items were brought into this cooler this morning during prep (approximately 5 hours ago). The foods were discarded to correct and the cooler should be monitored moving forward to ensure effective cold holding is taking place.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The egg wash (milk and eggs) on the prep line were observed holding around 60F in its ice bath. The ice is only touching the bottom of the inner pan and the pans are located between the grill and the fryers. The current set up does not allow for ice to surround the egg wash with the current equipment. Education was conducted with the PIC and staff. The current egg wash was discarded and a new set up with a larger ice pan and an egg wash pan that allows for the ice to surround ice will be used moving forward. Ensure that the ice is maintained at a level around the food that is higher than the level of the food. Monitor the egg wash temperatures throughout use times to ensure that effective cold holding is maintained at all times.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 

A pan of white sauce is observed in the right most prep cooler during the inspection. This pan came from a batch observed earlier in the inspection on a counter cooling and was observed at 60F-80F depending on where the internal temperature was observed. Education was conducted with the PIC. This equipment is not sufficient for cooling hot foods, especially while the cooler is in use for active food preparation. The pan was moved to the walk ins for rapid cooling. Stirring is also suggested because of the temperature gradient observed. Ensure that all foods are cooled effectively at all times in the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Two sections of the salad prep cooler are observed with the lids wedged open by items inside. Internal temperatures for lettuce and house made mayo based sauces are observed in the 51F-52F range. These items were brought into this section approximately 4 hours ago. The rest of the cooler appears to be functioning correctly and only the current situation (the lids remaining open) appears to be the issue. The sauces and lettuce were discarded to correct and the lids allowed to close to correct possible future concerns.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

The hand sink in the kitchen was observed being used to rinse off a utensil. The PIC was notified and instructed to review procedures for using a hand sink with staff. Ensure that hand sinks are only used for hand washing and no other tasks at any time.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The soap dispenser next to the prep line is not functioning during this inspection. The PIC indicated that it has been non-functioning for a couple days and there is not a temporary option at the sink at this time. A temporary dispenser was placed at the location to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival all of the sani buckets in the kitchen area registered low on the inspector's test strips. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets to correct the violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels while in use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The dish machine in the bar area did not register on the inspector’s test strips when checked. The PIC and inspector adjusted the machine for several minutes and eventually got it to operate correctly. Ensure that the machine is functioning correctly at all times. This is the third inspection in a row where an issue was found with this machine sanitizing food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) A single knife in the knife rack next to the salad prep area does not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage in the knife rack. 2) Multiple ladles in the hallway storage appear to have not been completely cleaned prior to storage. The kitchen manager was shown and moved the items back to dish to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage. This is the second inspection in a row where a dish cleaning violation has been noted.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The sink in the back section next to the ice machine is observed with a consistent leak coming from the faucet. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the item repaired prior to the follow up. The follow up is being scheduled for three business days to allow time for repairs to be made after the weekend.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code. 

A tray of cooling spaghetti noodles is observed with the noodle in contact with the shelf above. The kitchen manager was shown and instructed to store foods so that they are not in contact with soiled and un-sanitized equipment. Other storage options were discussed and the noodles discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are protected form contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Nozzles on the fountain drink machine in the Tuscan Room are observed soiled. This equipment has not been used today and the nozzles should have been cleaned after its last use. The PIC was notified and had the nozzles removed for cleaning and sanitizing to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean regularly.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives in the kitchen do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage in the knife rack. The kitchen manager was shown and moved the items back to dish to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple ice wands in the walk in freezer are observed soiled during this inspection. The kitchen manager was shown and moved the wands to dish for recleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact items remain clean prior to contact with foods.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival the bar, pizza and server area do not have a sani bucket ready for use in the area. The PIC was asked and made buckets for these areas to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer is available in the handling and preparation areas at all times that handling and preparation are taking place.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The dispenser for sanitizer used in the sani buckets does not appear to be functioning correctly at this time. Multiple buckets were ran and the solutions checked with both inspector and facility test strips. All came back without required color changes. As a temporary measure buckets will be made with the CL based bar sanitizer. The follow-up is to ensure that the equipment is worked on and begins to provide adequate sanitizer.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the dish machine in the bar would not register sanitizer on the inspector test strips. Troubleshooting was conducted by the PIC and the machine began to register sanitizer prior to the end of the inspection. Ensure that the sanitizers are maintained at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

1) Several house flies are observed throughout the food preparation and storage areas. 2) Numerous fruit flies are observed in the dry storage area and appear to be coming from a bag of onions. The PIC was consulted and instructed to contact pest control for help managing the situations. A follow-up is being scheduled for 10 days to verify that the issue is resolved. Inspecting incoming shipments was discussed.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. 

The employee entrance appears to have had the sweeper strips and other seals damaged and allowing for gaps in that are allowing the entrance of pests into the facility. Per the PIC a call has already been placed to see these repaired. Ensure that they are repaired prior to the next routine inspection. It is highly suggested that they be repaired soon to help manage the current pest issue.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor.

Multiple containers of sauces, soups and cooked pastas in the walk in cooler are without lids or other coverings. The PIC was consulted and the containers covered during this inspection to correct. Ensure that foods are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination.

1) A pan of steak knives in the kitchen is observed with food debris in the bottom of the container. 2) A glass with mixing utensils for drink in the bar is observed with a soiled container bottom. Both items were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that storage containers used for food contact utensils are maintained clean moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The ceilings vents throughout the kitchen and back hallway need cleaning both on the grates as well as on the tiles around the intakes. Clean prior to the next routine inspection and maintain clean moving forword.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The three part sink in the dish area needs to be re-sealed to the wall behind it. The PIC was consulted and caulking was suggested to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface and fill the gap currently observed. Ensure that all relevant areas are maintained easily cleanable.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Multiple locations throughout the facility are in need of cleaning. Items include: 1) shelves in the walk in cooler; 2) the fan cover in the walk in cooler; 3) the piping behind the cooling unit in the walk in cooler; 4) the shelf under the cook line in the kitchen. Ensure all areas are maintained clean and sanitary at all times in the locations with food preparation and storage.  The PIC was consulted and instructed to clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

Phones, drinks and keys were observed on multiple counters throughout the food preparation areas. Employees were not observed to be making use of any of these items during the walkthrough. Employee personal storage practices were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to stored these items in areas that do not pose a concern for food contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield on the ice machine is soiled and in need of cleaning. The location was shown to he PIC and the item cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.13: (A) Insect control devices used to stun or electrocute flying insects shall be designed to retain insect in device. (B) Devices shall be installed where it is not located over FOOD preparation area and dead insects and fragments cannot impel or fall into exposed FOOD or FOOD-EQUIPMENT. 

On arrival a live roach was observed in front of the pizza station. Dead insects were also observed on the reverse side of this wall. The PIC was aware of this issue and has already contacted their pest control agency (Presto-X) for remediation. Records were checked in the Presto-X binder and site visits took place on 1/11 and 1/19 (this morning). Spraying has already taken place and powders and traps placed throughout the facility. Fumigation of the inside of the wall surrounding the pizza station is being planned at this time and it has been taken out of service until the situation can be remediated. A follow up is being scheduled for two weeks. The inspector gave the PIC his card and instructed the facility to keep him up to date if extensions are needed as the situation is managed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Tile coving was damaged: 1) in a corner in the mop room to the right of the soda syrups and; 2) at the end of the wall projection next to the dish area hand sink.  Repair both locations prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The ceilings vents above the prep line need cleaning both on the grates as well as on the tiles around the intakes. Clean prior to the next routine inspection and maintain clean moving foreword.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Multiple sani buckets in the facility are observed with quat concentrations of 0-100 ppm. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The dish machine in the kitchen is only registering 25 ppm CL on either the inspector’s or the facility’s test strips. CL is required to be at a minimum of 50 ppm for effective sanitization. EcoLab was contacted during this inspection for maintenance. Follow up in three days for compliance. At this time, a sink with sanitizer can be substituted for sanitizing in the machine.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds. 

The bar dish machine does not have a sanitizer hooked up during this inspection. A jug of detergent was hooked up (and empty) in place of the sanitizer. PIC stated that a truck would be received in a day or two and sanitizer will be ensured to be on it. Follow up in three days for compliance. At this time, a sink with sanitizer can be substituted for sanitizing in the machine.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with using proper methods.

Time labels were not observed on multiple labels of cooling sauces in the walk in freezer. Education was conducted with the kitchen manager and they are aware that time markers should be used during the cooling process.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. 

Multiple moist cloths through the facility are observed stored on counters and not in solution. PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that the cloths are stored between uses in solution.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Sandwich toothpicks are stored in a small metal tub along with a pen. Pens are not considered a cleaned/sanitized surface and so should be stored so that they do not contaminate the food contact surfaces of single service items. The PIC was consulted and the pan removed. The toothpicks were discarded and the pen moved to correct the violation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

Multiple instances of not using a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing are observed throughout the inspection. Education conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that employees are properly washing hands throughout their shifts.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink next to the pizza prep station is without paper towels at this time. This is the only sink near this location that can be easily/ conveniently accessed. Paper towels were replaced during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

Black, brown and pink slime is observed on the deflector shield of the ice machine in the back of the facility. PIC is instructed to maintain clean at all times. The shield was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Multiple sani buckets in the facility are observed with quat concentrations of 0-50 ppm. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

A quarter pan of water/chicken is being hot held on the right most grill. The chicken is observed with internal temperatures of 120-130F and the water is observed at approximately 118F. PIC stated that the chicken was prepared approximately 30 minutes ago at the time of this inspection. The tray was moved closer to the burners to warm the chicken up to hot holding temperatures (135F or higher).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

1) The ceilings vents above the prep line need cleaning around them (dust); 2) the hot lamp shelves used for ready to serve orders along the prep line is in need of cleaning (dust); 3) ice in the walk in cooler behind the condenser is needing to be cleaned/ removed; 4) dust is needed to be cleaned from the front of the condenser in the walk in cooler as well as along the roof and light fixture. PIC was consulted for all of these areas and they are instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain the surfaces clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Multiple instances of improper handwashing procedure observed: two instances of quick rinses rather than 20 seconds of handwashing; and five instances of failure to use a barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands. CORRECTED- Provided education and discussed with PIC. Review handwashing procedure with all staff.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Out of temperature foods observed in the top portions of two prep coolers. Both coolers were observed with lids open upon inspector’s arrival. Discussed keeping lids closed as foods in the lower portions of the coolers were well within safe temperatures. Discussed the benefits of temperature logs. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded.
SALAD PREP: two pans of shredded cheese at 50F, two small pans of shredded cheese at 50F and 64F, a small pan of dressing at 64F, and bottles of ranch (56F), aioli (62F), and chipotle mayo (60F) were voluntarily discarded.
COOKLINE PREP #1: shredded cheese at 49F and 51F and minced garlic at 54F were voluntarily discarded. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A spray bottle of peroxide sanitizer observed stored on the shelf above the back prep counter. CORRECTED- Bottle was moved to storage away from food prep and storage.
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed soiled/dusty ceiling tiles above the cookline. Observed soil accumulation on a box fan used along the cookline. Clean to protect food from potential contamination during preparation and storage.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [P]
3-305.14: During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Dish machine observed with 0ppm Cl. PIC had noticed this morning and placed a call to EcoLab for service, but continued use of the dish machine under the impression that it was reaching a sanitizing temperature. Per inspector’s plate thermometer, dish machine reached 122F, insufficient to sanitize dishes. CORRECTED— Dishwasher will set up a section of the three compartment sink to sanitize dishes using quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum concentration (50-200ppm). [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Shrimp and fish observed thawing in containers of standing water near the back prep sink. CORRECTED— Both observed below 41F. Discussed with PIC, who adjusted to have cool running water.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Salmon was observed in the walk-in cooler thawed while still sealed in reduced-oxygen packaging. Packaging states to remove all packaging and thaw under refrigeration. Remove or break ROP to thaw according to the 2017 FDA Food Code or manufacturer label.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. [C]
